I'm continuing research for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Jira project key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net, board id 500 "SFCC board"). This refines an earlier investigation — new information just surfaced that changes the target.

Background: A Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937) shows a boutique-related panel with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" calendar grid, an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with time-slot buttons, and a "CONTINUE" button. It's filed under a "Find in Boutique" grouping in the Figma layers panel. I'd previously hypothesized this was Booxi appointment-booking (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor already documented in Jira for read-only appointment history in My Account — tickets SFCC-72, SFCC-626, epic SFCC-16), since nothing about "Find in Boutique" as documented (a pure per-boutique stock-check flyout, no dates/times — Jira SFCC-297/308/458/307) matched the screen.

**New information just confirmed by the project's frontend lead (a direct participant, not a guess):** this screen is specifically the **"Find in Boutique" → "Book a Fitting" flow/modal** — i.e., there's a specific named sub-flow called "Book a Fitting" that this calendar belongs to. My previous Jira searches used "calendar", "date picker", "Booxi", "appointment", "Find in Boutique" — never the word "fitting" — so this may surface a ticket I completely missed.

Also newly revealed: a Figma comment thread on this exact screen, from a sticky note reading "Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar", authored by **Charmaine Lew**, posted "12 days ago" (so approximately 2026-07-30, given today is 2026-08-11), tagging/mentioning **Kiera Rikard-Bell** and **Marcel Angelo N. Navarro** (the frontend lead), with "1 reply" already in that thread (content not visible to me).

Please research Jira (project SFCC) and report back on:

1. **"Book a Fitting" / "fitting" directly.** Search broadly: `text ~ "fitting"`, `text ~ "Book a Fitting"`, `text ~ "fitting appointment"`. Report every hit — ticket key, summary, status, epic parent, and quote the relevant part of the description/AC/comments describing what this flow is, what backend/system it calls (Booxi? something else?), and whether it's in-storefront self-service booking or an external/chat-handoff pattern.

2. **Charmaine Lew** — check if she appears as a reporter, assignee, or commenter on any ticket (especially design/UX-adjacent ones, or anything related to Find in Boutique, Booxi, appointments, or fittings). Try jira_get_user_profile if you can find her account, and pull any tickets she's active on relating to this topic.

3. **Kiera Rikard-Bell** — same treatment. A prior pass found a bare first name "Kiera" mentioned in SFCC-255 (size-selector/"Find My Size" copy) and SFCC-236 (Recently Viewed product-card) — check whether those tie back to a "Book a Fitting" or sizing-adjacent context now that her surname is known, or whether they're genuinely unrelated as previously assessed.

4. **Re-check Find in Boutique epic/tickets for a "Book a Fitting" sub-story** — re-pull SFCC-297, SFCC-308, SFCC-458, and their parent epic (SFCC-5 PDP or wherever Find in Boutique sits) and check for any child/linked ticket specifically about booking a fitting, in case it exists as a sibling story not caught by a generic "Find in Boutique" text search before.

5. **Any ticket connecting "Book a Fitting" to Booxi specifically**, or to a different/new system — e.g. check if "Personal Styling" (previously found referenced in SFCC-626, "My Account – Services Page Layout," which mentioned a "Personal Styling tile with 'Book an Appointment' link routing to Booxi") is the same concept as "Book a Fitting," a sibling concept, or unrelated.

Report back with concrete ticket keys, summaries, statuses, and direct quotes — I need to know whether "Book a Fitting" is a real, already-ticketed feature I simply hadn't searched for correctly, or whether it's genuinely new/undocumented in Jira. This is read-only research — do not modify, comment on, or transition any Jira issues. Keep the report focused and organized under the 5 numbered questions; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing an answer, not an end user directly.

## Research Report: "Book a Fitting" / Charmaine Lew / Kiera Rikard-Bell in Jira (project SFCC)

### 1. "Book a Fitting" / "fitting" — direct search results

**No ticket in the SFCC project documents a "Book a Fitting" flow.** Every search angle came up empty or returned false positives:

- `text ~ "fitting"` → 14 hits, all false positives from Jira's stemming (matches "Fit"/"Fitted"/"fits" anywhere in text): PDP slide-out stories, SEO tickets, `Ask Charmaine...` subtasks, spikes, etc. None describe a booking flow.
- `text ~ "Book a Fitting"` → **one hit**, **SFCC-247** ("Spike: Validate Magento Product Hierarchy Against SFCC Variation Model", Done). This looked significant at first, but reading the full comment shows it's a pure false positive from JQL's term-matching (not true phrase-matching): the comment contains "**price books**" (G3–G7 gap list) and "**Fitted** Blouse" (product example name) — i.e., stemmed "book" + stemmed "fit" appearing independently, nothing about appointment booking. **This is not a real hit.**
- `text ~ "fitting appointment"` → 0 hits.
- `summary ~ "fitting"` (narrower) → only SFCC-207 (Charmaine accordion-tabs subtask, matched on "does not seem to **fit** in current design") and SFCC-102 "PDP – Slide Out - **Size & Fit**" — neither is booking-related.
- `cf[10231] ~ "fitting"` (searching the separate **Acceptance Criteria** custom field, `customfield_10231`, which the default `text ~` search does **not** index) → same false positives (SFCC-266, SFCC-195, SFCC-102, SFCC-90), all stemming noise, nothing new.
- `cf[10231] ~ "Booxi" OR "Booksy" OR "calendar" OR "appointment"` → **zero hits, project-wide.** No Acceptance Criteria anywhere in SFCC mentions any of these terms.
- Synonym sweep (`consultation`, `styling session`, `schedule`, `book now`, `reserve a fitting`) → 33 hits, all false positives (Global-e jobs, category scheduling, opening-hours feeds, etc.) — nothing related.
- Recent-ticket sweep (all PDP/Store Locator children created in the last 14 days) → 33 tickets, all granular Store Detail/Locator UI stories (hours table, map, contact block, etc.) or standard PDP stories (wishlist, Find in Boutique, Shipping & Returns) — no booking/calendar/fitting title.

**Conclusion: "Book a Fitting" is not an existing Jira ticket, story, or AC anywhere in the SFCC project — under any wording I could construct.**

### 2. Charmaine Lew

Confirmed as a **real, resolvable Jira user**: `jira_get_user_profile` succeeded on `charmaine.lew@accenture.com` → display name "Charmaine Lew". She does **not** appear as an assignee or reporter anywhere — she's referenced only as a third-party design contact inside subtask titles/comments authored by the dev team:

- **SFCC-207** — "Ask Charmaine on how accordion tabs work in desktop design (can be up to 7 times, does not seem to fit in current design)" (Done; subtask of **SFCC-195** "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care", parent epic SFCC-5 PDP). Comment by Dani Rivett: *"Charmaine has added a gradient to show more items horizontally"*.
- **SFCC-211** — "Ask Charmaine to design error messaging on PDP - max purchase quantity" (Done; subtask of SFCC-196 "PDP UI – Maximum Purchase Quantity").
- **SFCC-208** — "Discuss the to-be Chat functionality with Rebecca - then with Charmaine on how that should function, where and when chat should appear / position on each page" (To Do; subtask of SFCC-267 "PDP – Slide Out – Shipping & Returns and Assistance").
- Also turned up (via broader text match, not opened in full) in several other PDP/PLP ticket comment threads: SFCC-203, SFCC-199, SFCC-194, SFCC-150, SFCC-92, SFCC-28.

**Assessment:** Charmaine Lew is an established, actively-engaged UX/UI designer specifically on PDP-related design decisions (accordion behaviour, error messaging, chat placement) around the same period as the Figma comment (subtasks created 2026-07-21, close to the "~12 days ago" comment date). Nothing in these tickets mentions fitting, Booxi, or a calendar — but she is clearly a legitimate, active design authority the frontend lead would expect to see commenting on a PDP-adjacent Figma screen.

### 3. Kiera Rikard-Bell

Also confirmed as a **real, resolvable Jira user**: `kiera.rikard-bell@accenture.com` → display name "Kiera Rikard-Bell". Same pattern as Charmaine — no assignee/reporter role, only referenced by first name in comments:

- **SFCC-255** — "Discuss Size Selector - Recommendation in design review Friday" (In Progress; subtask of **SFCC-101** "PDP – Slide out - Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA"). Comment by Jasmijn Tsang: *"had a chat with Kiera and User:712020:c99d37b3-9c93-4347-951d-5ffb32ff1341 yesterday - the idea is now to have 'Recommended: 2' displayed on PDP next to the size selector, replacing 'Find My Size'..."*
- **SFCC-236** — "Product Card Shared Component" (Ready For Review; under SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components). Comment: *"The product card behaviour on the 'see full recently viewed' page was not specified in the design - I asked Kiera - she recommended to keep the behaviour similar to product card on PLP."*
- **SFCC-648** — "pdp/size-selector" (To Do; under SFCC-2) also matched the `Kiera` text search, but its description/comments show no visible "Kiera" mention — likely a search artifact, not a genuine reference. Treat as inconclusive.

**Assessment:** This re-confirms (rather than overturns) the prior pass's finding — SFCC-255 and SFCC-236 are about **PDP sizing UX** (size-selector recommendation wording, product-card behaviour), not Find in Boutique or fitting appointments. They remain genuinely separate from a "Book a Fitting" flow. However, her role — giving UX direction on PDP-adjacent shopper-facing copy/behaviour decisions — is entirely consistent with also being the right person to consult on a Find-in-Boutique/Book-a-Fitting screen; there's just no ticket connecting her to that specific flow.

### 4. Find in Boutique epic/tickets — re-pulled, no "Book a Fitting" sibling found

"Find in Boutique" is **not a single epic** — it's a cross-cutting feature split across three different epics, confirmed by re-pulling all three stories plus their parents and issue links:

- **SFCC-297** "PDP UI — Find in Boutique Button and Slide-In Panel" (In Refinement; parent **SFCC-5** PDP epic). Description: *"This story covers the PWA Kit frontend component for Find in Boutique on the PDP. It includes the Find in Boutique button display on eligible products, the modal/flyout UI showing per-boutique stock availability for the selected size, and all boutique availability states. The real-time OMS call to NewStore via MuleSoft and response caching logic are out of scope — covered in SFCC-308."* Its full 12-point Acceptance Criteria (in `customfield_10231`, not previously visible via description alone) is exclusively about: product image/name/colour/price display, a **size selector for stock-checking** (not booking), per-boutique Available/Low Stock/Out of Stock states, expand/collapse boutique details (hours, phone, email, map, directions), geolocation/location search, empty state, and a mobile slide-up panel. **No calendar, no time slots, no booking confirmation step, no signed-in-customer-name display** — nothing resembling the Figma screen.
- **SFCC-308** "Inventory – Real-Time Boutique Stock Check for Find in Boutique" (To Do; parent **SFCC-307** Inventory epic). Purely the NewStore-via-MuleSoft real-time stock integration layer. Linked to SFCC-297 via "Relates".
- **SFCC-458** "Find in Boutique – Buffer Stock Exclusion Logic" (To Do; parent **SFCC-15** Order Management epic). Purely about excluding buffer-stock deduction from the Find in Boutique availability figure. Depends on SFCC-297, SFCC-456, SFCC-11.
- The **SFCC-9** "Store Locator" epic description explicitly scopes Find in Boutique the same way: *"Find in Boutique: real-time stock availability per boutique for a product in context on the store detail page"* (In Scope), and lists *"Find in Boutique slide-out on PDP — covered in SFCC-5"* under Out of Scope (i.e., cross-references SFCC-297, confirming no other Find in Boutique variant exists).

**No child/linked/sibling ticket about booking a fitting exists anywhere under any of these three parent epics.** The feature as ticketed today is stock-check-only, exactly as previously understood.

### 5. Booxi / Booksy / Personal Styling — and a genuine naming inconsistency

"Personal Styling" and "Find in Boutique" are **confirmed as two separate, unrelated concepts** in the current backlog — but a real documentation inconsistency surfaced around the appointment vendor's name:

- **SFCC-16** "Customer Account & CRM" (Epic). Its own description says, in three separate places: *"Appointments section within My Account (**Booksy** integration — storefront scope and timelines TBC)"*; *"**Booksy** — appointment data source for My Account appointments section (scope TBC)"*; *"**Booksy** platform configuration — Zimmermann scope"* (Out of Scope); and *"Appointments section storefront scope and delivery timelines are **TBC** pending further scoping with Zimmermann"* (Assumptions).
- **SFCC-72** "**Booxi** Appointment History Integration" (To Do; child of SFCC-16). Description: *"Placeholder story - appointment history sourced from Booxi API."* Read-only history only — matches your prior understanding.
- **SFCC-626** "My Account – Services Page Layout" (To Do; child of SFCC-16). Description: *"...Personal Styling tile with 'Book an Appointment' link (**routes to Booxi** — dependency: SFCC-72), Gift Cards tile..., and Care Guides tile. The Appointments section is built as a **placeholder** to accommodate the Booxi integration (SFCC-72) **without requiring structural redesign when it is ready**."* Acceptance Criteria field is null (unrefined).
- **SFCC-525** "Store Detail – Boutique Services Section" (To Do; child of **SFCC-9** Store Locator, not SFCC-16). Description: *"...Each service is presented as a tile containing a service heading, a short description, and a CTA link (e.g. 'Book an Appointment' for Personal Styling, 'Make a Reservation' for Click and Reserve)."* Same CTA-link pattern, surfaced on the Store Detail page instead of My Account. Acceptance Criteria field is also null.

**So: the epic (SFCC-16) says "Booksy," while both of its own child stories (SFCC-72, SFCC-626) say "Booxi."** These are two different real-world commercial products (Booxi = retail/luxury appointment-booking and clienteling platform; Booksy = salon/beauty booking app) — this is either a straightforward, uncorrected typo in the epic description, or a genuine unresolved ambiguity about which vendor is actually contracted. Either way, it has never been reconciled in Jira, and it's directly relevant to your Figma sticky-note finding (Charmaine Lew's *"Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar"*) — that comment reads as exactly this same open question (is the calendar Booxi/Booksy's own out-of-the-box hosted widget, vs. something Zimmermann must build?), still unresolved anywhere in Jira.

**Critically: every "Book an Appointment" reference found (SFCC-16, SFCC-72, SFCC-626, SFCC-525) describes a CTA link that routes externally to Booxi/Booksy** — not an embedded native calendar+time-slot+Continue-button UI. Both stub stories (SFCC-626, SFCC-525) have zero Acceptance Criteria written, and the epic (SFCC-16) explicitly flags the whole Appointments section as **"TBC"**. This "Book an Appointment" concept also lives under **My Account** and the **Store Detail page** — never under PDP or "Find in Boutique."

### Bottom line

"Book a Fitting" as a PDP → Find in Boutique sub-flow with an in-storefront calendar/time-slot/Continue booking UI **does not exist as a ticket, story, AC, or even a passing text mention anywhere in Jira** — this was checked via full-text search, the separate Acceptance Criteria custom field, synonym variations, and a 14-day recency sweep. The closest conceptual relative already ticketed is "Personal Styling → Book an Appointment" (SFCC-16/72/626/525), but that is scoped to My Account and Store Detail pages as an external link/placeholder to Booxi (per SFCC-72/626) or "Booksy" (per SFCC-16 itself) — not PDP/Find-in-Boutique, not an embedded calendar, and explicitly still "TBC." The frontend lead's confirmation that this Figma screen is specifically "Find in Boutique → Book a Fitting" describes a linkage that is genuinely new/undocumented in Jira as of today (2026-08-11) — the Figma comment thread (Charmaine Lew, ~2026-07-30, tagging Kiera Rikard-Bell and the frontend lead, 1 reply not visible to this research) currently appears to be the only record of this decision anywhere, and it lives in Figma, not Jira.
